# Didache Chapter 16 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Hierosolymitanus (H), Didache 16 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/DID_016_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 16

**1** Watch your life. Keep your lamps lit. Keep your belts buckled. Stay ready — because you have no idea what hour our Lord is coming.

**2** Gather together often. Seek what nourishes your souls. Because all the years you've spent in faith will count for nothing if you don't hold on to the very end.

**3** In the last days, false prophets and people who destroy will multiply. The sheep will become wolves. Love will become hate.

**4** As lawlessness runs wild, people will betray one another, hate one another, hand one another over to their enemies. And then — the world-deceiver will appear, claiming to be a son of God. He will perform signs and wonders. The earth will be handed over to him. He will do things more lawless than anything since creation.

**5** Then everyone will be thrown into the fire of testing. Many will fall and be destroyed. But those who hold out — those who keep faith to the end — will be saved by the One who bore the curse.

**6** And then the signs of truth will break through: first — a sign: an opening torn in the sky. Then — the sound of a trumpet. Then — the resurrection of the dead.

**7** But not all the dead. As was said: "The Lord will come, and all his holy ones with him."

**8** Then the whole world will see the Lord — coming on the clouds of heaven.

---

*PNEUMA note: The Didache ends where it began — with a stark choice, but now cosmic in scale. The Two Ways that opened chs. 1-5 (life and death) here become a final eschatological test: those who endure will be saved, those who don't will perish. The "world-deceiver" (κοσμοπλάνης) is the Antichrist of early Christian tradition. V.5's "saved by the One who bore the curse" — if this is Christ — is a flash of atonement theology in an otherwise practical document. And the ending is not a prayer or a benediction. It is a vision: the Lord, coming on the clouds. The Didache ends looking up.*
